name: NaturalReader
subcategory: synthetic voice, dubbing and AI avatars
tagline: Read user-provided text and documents aloud with a small set of licensed or local voices

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited system Free Voices; 20,000 Lite-voice characters/day; 4,000 shared Plus/Cloned characters/day; no MP3 conversion or OCR.

tiers.name: Lite
tiers.limits: Unlimited Lite listening; 1,000,000 Lite-voice MP3 characters/month; no Plus/Pro voices or voice cloning.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: 500,000 shared Plus/Cloned listening characters/day; 1,000,000 Lite MP3 characters/month + 1,000,000 shared Plus/Cloned MP3 characters/month; clone up to 2 voices.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 500,000 shared Plus/Cloned/Pro listening characters/day; 1,000,000 Lite MP3 characters/month + 1,000,000 shared premium MP3 characters/month; clone up to 2 voices.

tiers.name: Lite EDU
tiers.notes: Annual-only; price field is the effective monthly cost of the 50-user starting package, not a per-user rate.

tiers.name: Plus EDU
tiers.limits: Annual packages: 5 users $299; 10 $499; 20 $899; 30 $1,200; 40 $1,400; 50 $1,500; above 50 starts at $25/user/year.
tiers.notes: Annual-only; price field is the effective monthly cost of the 5-user starting package.

tiers.name: Site License
tiers.notes: Annual-only; pricing is based on total enrollment.

pricing.freeTierCaps: unlimited system voices; 20,000 Lite-voice characters/day; 4,000 Plus/Cloned characters/day; no MP3 or OCR
pricing.billingTerms: individual plans are monthly + annual; EDU and Site License plans are annual-only
pricing.hiddenCosts: Audio made under Personal/EDU plans is licensed for personal use only; commercial rights require the separately billed Commercial AI Voice Generator. App Store/Google Play prices, taxes, and regional fees can differ.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For NaturalReader, read user-provided text and documents aloud with a small set of licensed or local voices. The hard boundary is voice catalog, ocr, document formats, mobile apps, and commercial licensing options, plus models, compute, rights, and safety operations.
coreLoopDIY: Read user-provided text and documents aloud with a small set of licensed or local voices, clearly labeling synthetic audio and retaining provenance for every output.
requirements: voices the user has rights and consent to use
whatYouLose: voice catalog, OCR, document formats, mobile apps, and commercial licensing options
moderation, consent verification, and enterprise rights
moatNotes: models, compute, rights, and safety operations
ongoingBurden: model licensing, consent records, impersonation risk, watermarking, GPU queues, media storage, abuse response, and rapid model changes
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for NaturalReader because customers pay for output quality, production speed, licensed voices, consent workflows, and a provider that carries the operational risk. The recurring cost buys model licensing, consent records, impersonation risk, watermarking, GPU queues, media storage, abuse response, and rapid model changes, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Piper
priorArt.desc: Active community continuation of the fast local Piper text-to-speech engine.

alternatives.name: Balabolka
alternatives.desc: Opens most document formats, reads them with whatever voices Windows owns, and never discovers a subscription.

facts.install: Run the Windows installer or unzip the portable build
facts.engines: Microsoft Speech API 4/5 and Microsoft Speech Platform voices installed on Windows; an optional separate utility can call online TTS services
facts.dataFormat: Input documents and generated WAV, MP3, MP4, OGG or WMA audio plus optional LRC/SRT files on local disk
facts.gapVsPaid: It is Windows-only, visually dated and limited to installed voices, with none of NaturalReader's polished cross-device premium-voice experience.
facts.setupBlocker: Balabolka includes no voices, so the desired Windows SAPI voice or language pack must already be installed

alternatives.name: Koodo Reader
alternatives.desc: Reads nearly every ebook format aloud; the fancy hosted voice is paid, the local and system voices are not.

facts.install: Install a desktop/mobile package from the site or app store; Windows also offers portable builds
facts.engines: Free read-aloud uses the operating-system TTS engine or browser voices; Koodo's hosted AI voice is a paid Pro feature
facts.dataFormat: Books, covers, configuration, progress and annotations in a local library folder/app data or browser cache; free users do not upload reading data
facts.gapVsPaid: It is ebook-centric and weaker for arbitrary documents, OCR and browser-based reading than NaturalReader.
facts.setupBlocker: The macOS desktop build may need Open Anyway, while Linux read-aloud depends on a working system or browser speech engine

alternatives.name: Readest
alternatives.desc: A book-and-PDF reader with built-in narration and no premium-voice bait-and-switch.

facts.install: Install from an app store, the site/GitHub releases or Flathub, or use the hosted web app
facts.engines: Native OS TTS on Android/iOS, Web Speech API in the web app, and Microsoft Edge TTS cloud voices on supported platforms
facts.dataFormat: A local app library/cache plus optional Readest Cloud sync for books, progress, highlights and notes; exportable library backup ZIP; credentials can be end-to-end encrypted
facts.gapVsPaid: It is primarily an ebook reader, with desktop narration relying on browser or cloud voices and no comparable OCR workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Desktop native voices are not yet wired up, so desktop users need Edge TTS or browser voices; Windows may also need WebView2

alternatives.name: Thorium Reader
alternatives.desc: A free desktop reader built by accessibility people: ebooks, PDFs and text-to-speech, with no account or ad slot.

facts.install: Install from Microsoft Store or use the official Windows installer, macOS build, AppImage or Debian package
facts.engines: Operating-system text-to-speech voices selected according to the publication's language
facts.dataFormat: Imported publications in Thorium's local application-data publications directory; bookmarks/highlights in local state and a dedicated SQLite notes database in recent versions
facts.gapVsPaid: Read-aloud is EPUB-focused and does not work for PDFs, a major limitation beside NaturalReader's document coverage.
facts.setupBlocker: A corresponding operating-system voice pack must be installed for any missing language

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Personal plan and a clearly labeled local synthetic-media tool DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for NaturalReader in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite, ffmpeg, and a user-owned local TTS model; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: read user-provided text and documents aloud with a small set of licensed or local voices, clearly labeling synthetic audio and retaining provenance for every output.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Require a project-level rights and consent acknowledgement before generating audio.
Ship with no celebrity, public-figure, or scraped voice assets and accept only explicitly licensed models.
Generate speech from text with voice, speed, pause, pronunciation, and segment controls.
Create a timeline for audio, captions, uploaded visuals, and simple transitions.
Embed project metadata and a visible synthetic-media disclosure in exported assets.
Store prompts, model identifiers, consent notes, and output hashes in a local provenance log.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out cloning a voice without clear consent.
Deliberately leave out impersonation or deceptive unlabeled media.
Deliberately leave out a frontier avatar model, public hosting, or enterprise rights clearance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
